intended_use: Preregistered public development corpus for the Codex-only three-arm comparison. Its cases are built so that the deciding rule often lives in the full reviewer workflow references rather than in the pattern catalog alone. It is not sealed and does not establish generalization.
contamination_risk: The corpus is inspectable and was written by the same author who wrote the reviewer references it exercises. Every result must disclose that exposure and remain development evidence.

labeling.procedure: Single-author labels written from the reviewer references at the frozen skill commit, before any model call on this corpus. Every label records the reference rule that decides it, and every case records which prompt arm is expected to get it right and why. After authoring, a Claude subagent and Codex gpt-5.6-sol each labeled all 30 cases blind from the contracts alone. 66 of 74 author labels matched both. An arbiter subagent resolved the 8 disputed labels and 2 extra findings from quoted contract text; the user approved the resolutions on 2026-09-26.
labeling.limitations: Labels were authored by one agent and then checked by two blind labelers and an arbiter; all are models, not human experts. No model has been run on the corpus. Optional labels mark contract boundaries where the references do not force one verdict. Code is synthetic and original; field themes were reduced to structure only.
labeling.instance_severities: Two labels use an instance severity that the references define but the Quick Reference does not list: #1 at P1 when one promised outcome is verified and another is not, and #23 at P0 when a guard-suppressed render lets a negative assertion pass.
